before:
Fen Drainage Board — Winter Pump Allocation Bulletin

When inflow exceeds the station's rated throughput, the duty operator must distribute the available capacity across the three registered land classes. Any class may be served in any volume, and no class may be left wholly unserved for longer than forty-eight hours. In deciding where the surplus goes while a backlog stands, the operator serves market gardens ahead of grazing marsh, and grazing marsh ahead of amenity ground. Nothing in this bulletin alters what the operator is permitted to do at the sluice; it settles only which claim yields when two are pressed in the same hour. Operators log each allocation against the gauge reading taken at the hour of decision, and countersign the sheet before leaving the station.

before:
County Herbarium — Loan Catalogue, Preliminary Note

The catalogue that follows lists sheets held in the upper store, arranged by collector and then by year of gathering. Sheets marked with a bracketed T are the herbarium's own type material, gathered chiefly in the coastal dunes between 1902 and 1931. Type sheets may be consulted in the reading room and may also be lent to accredited institutions on the usual fourteen-day terms. All other sheets travel freely within the county museum circuit. Requests are made on the green form, countersigned by the honorary curator, and returned to the store clerk, who enters the movement in the day book before the sheet leaves its cabinet.
after:

before:

Staff are respectfully requested to ensure that the serving hatch remains unobstructed throughout each sitting. Trays waiting to go back should be stacked on the low shelf by the scullery door rather than on the counter itself, where they block the till. Urns are refilled between sittings and not during them. before:
Estuary Tide Gauge — Observer's Log, Sheet 44

Night watch, fourth of March. Wind west-north-west, moderate, glass falling slowly. The float trace ran smooth until 03:40, when the pen stepped up by 0.42 m over roughly four minutes and then settled to the predicted curve within the half hour. The stilling well was clear at the evening check and no vessel movement was logged in the reach. The observer is confident that the step reflects a true water movement rather than a fault in the float linkage. Trace annotated in red at the step and the sheet initialled. Morning watch asked to compare against the harbour office pressure record before the sheet is filed.

before:
Marsh Lane Allotment Society — Bonfire Policy

Burning on the site is governed by the district byelaw made in 1974 and last amended in 1998, which the committee summarises here for the convenience of tenants. Under that byelaw no fire may be lit between the first of April and the thirtieth of September, and no fire may be left unattended at any time. Tenants must burn only material grown on their own plot. The committee adds no requirement of its own beyond asking that neighbours on the windward side be told the evening before. Copies of the byelaw as amended are kept in the shed and may be photocopied on request.

before:
Goods Depot Handheld — Stocktake Sequence Settings

This sheet records the settings loaded onto the depot's four handheld terminals at the start of each count. Every listed operation is compulsory and none may be skipped by the counter; the sheet fixes only the order in which the terminal presents them.

    device_group = depot_handheld_4
    sequence = zero_scanner, sweep_bay, key_counts, print_slip
    idle_timeout_minutes = 12
    supervisor_override = enabled

Where the terminal loses power mid-count, the sequence resumes at the operation last completed rather than at the beginning. Amended sheets are dated and initialled by the stores supervisor, and the superseded sheet is kept in the folder behind the current one.

before:
Loch Ferry Service — Fuel Surcharge Computation

The surcharge added to each single fare is worked out afresh each quarter by the traffic clerk and posted at both slipways a fortnight before it takes effect. The clerk derives the figure by applying the twelve-month rolling mean of the gazetted marine gas oil index to the vessel's certified consumption per crossing, then dividing by the average loaded passenger count for the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The result is rounded up to the nearest five pence. Concession fares carry the same surcharge as full fares. The computation sheet is retained for three years and shown to the harbour committee on request.
after:
Loch Ferry Service — Fuel Surcharge Computation

The surcharge added to each single fare is worked out afresh each quarter by the traffic clerk and posted at both slipways a fortnight before it takes effect. The clerk derives the figure by applying the quarter-end spot value of the gazetted marine gas oil index to the vessel's certified consumption per crossing, then dividing by the average loaded passenger count for the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The result is rounded up to the nearest five pence. Concession fares carry the same surcharge as full fares. The computation sheet is retained for three years and shown to the harbour committee on request.
variation_site: The passage setting out how the traffic clerk arrives at the quarterly figure.
author_note: Swaps which formula is applied to derive the surcharge; the obligations, roundings and retention terms are all preserved.

before:
Parish Burial Registry — Field Encoding Note for Transcribers

Volunteers transcribing the older interment books enter one grave per line into the spreadsheet supplied. Surname goes in the first column in capitals, forename in the second as written, and the plot reference in the third exactly as it appears on the plan. Dates of interment are entered as day, month and year separated by solidus, with the year in four figures. Where the book gives only a month, the day column is left empty rather than filled with a zero. Illegible entries are flagged with a hash in the final column and referred to the parish clerk, who checks them against the faculty papers.

before:
Municipal Aquarium — Life Support Operator's Manual, Section 9

The chiller serving the cold-water hall runs continuously and holds the reef sump within half a degree of its posted figure. Trend charts are printed at each shift change and pinned by the door. The night duty operator must obtain the curator's authorisation before altering the chiller setpoint, whatever the trend chart shows. Alarm silencing is a separate matter and may be done at the panel without reference to anyone. Where authorisation cannot be got, the operator raises the header tank flow instead and notes the time. The manual is reissued each January and the superseded copy destroyed by the technical officer.
